newsitem.title: USA: Solv-Ex gets patent for electrolytic cell.
newsitem.headline: Solv-Ex gets patent for electrolytic cell.

text.p: Solv-Ex Corp. said on Tuesday a U.S. Patent had been issued for its new electrolytic cell for production of aluminum.
"Our efforts in the immediate future will be to achieve contiguous operation of the cell," Solv-Ex Chairman and Chief Executive Officer John Rendall said in a statement.
"Our objective is to have a prototype cell operational in the field during 1997 followed by full scale commercial production in 1998," he said.
This process was first successfully tested in January, the company said in a statement.

"We have made significant headway in confirming the ability to utilize non-consummable anodes on a consistent basis," Randall said. "This is in part due to the relatively low temperature at which the cell operates. The lower temperature also results in a significant savings in electricity as compared to conventional Hall-Herault cells."
Randall said the next step for the company was to make decisions about construction materials, metal collection and other design features for the first operational cell.
The company previously received a U.S. patent for the basic sulfuric acid leach technology used to extract alumina from the fine clay of Athabasca oil sands.
Applications for companion patents were pending in Canada and other countries for both of these patents, Solv-Ex said.
